Container.Name: AutoExtract
Container.Overview: Scans a folder on a schedule and automatically extracts zip, rar, 7z and tar archives (including multi-part sets and archives inside archives) into the folder they are in, then deletes the processed archives and junk files such as *.diz, or moves them to a trash folder. Web UI with live status, settings, scan history, statistics and themes. Created entirely by AI (Claude). It has been tested, but not in every situation - do your own due diligence before relying on it with data you cannot replace, and before exposing it to the internet.
Container.Changes:
Build 32, published 2026-11-21.
### 2026-11-21 - **Permissions:** extracted files and folders now get your permissions (and owner) before they appear in the folder. Before, they showed up with root's defaults (folders `drwxr-xr-x`, files `-rw-r--r--` or `-rw-------`) until the whole folder was finished, and the hidden work folder was root-only - Syncthing and other apps running as 99:100 reported permission errors on them. - **Also set the owner** (99:100, nobody:users) is now on for new installs. Existing installs keep their setting - turn it on in Settings if other apps (e.g. Syncthing) work on the extracted files.
### 2026-11-08 - **Folder per archive:** an archive that only holds pieces of other archives (for example `release1.zip` ... `release20.zip`, each holding one `release.partNN.rar`) is now extracted in place, so the pieces stay together and the set can be extracted. If some archives in the folder are still too new, the set waits until they are ready.
### 2026-11-07 - New setting **Folder per archive** (default **Smart**). An archive whose contents have no single top folder is now extracted into a folder named after the archive, so ten archives of loose files in one folder no longer end up mixed together. An archive that already holds one folder, or sits alone in a folder named like it (a release folder), is extracted as before. Choose **Always** or **Never** to force either way. Existing installs get Smart; it also applies to nested archives and **Extract folder…**.
### 2026-11-06 - **Cancel** button for each archive being extracted: stops that archive only, throws its partly extracted files away and leaves the archive as it was, while the others carry on. Scheduled scans skip a cancelled archive until it changes; Run now or Extract folder… tries it again. - Folder pickers and **Extract folder…** only show folders mapped into the container (`/downloads`, `/trash`, `/mnt/user`, ...); container folders such as `/var` are hidden, and the app data folder too. - Files dated in the future (for example from a clock or timezone mix-up) no longer count as "too new" forever. The time they arrived on the server is used instead, and the log shows a warning. - With **Overwrite** off, an archive is now kept when any of its files were skipped because they already exist, so nothing is lost. The log says how many files were skipped. - New **Keep** action for archives and junk. It is the default on a fresh install when there is no trash folder and no reachable Recycle Bin; existing settings are unchanged. - Kept archives, and archives left in place because their files already existed, are remembered: scheduled scans and Run now no longer extract them again until the archive changes, the action is changed or Overwrite is turned on. **Extract folder…** still extracts them. - Archives that fail even when retried on their own are remembered too: scheduled scans skip them until they change, Run now tries them again. Status and History show a "skipped" count. - Archives skipped because they were cancelled earlier now count as done, so "remaining" reaches 0. - An unexpected error on one archive no longer stops the whole scan. - A dry run no longer deletes leftover work folders, and **Extract folder…** refuses `/`. - Settings: the "Where your folders are on the server" box updates as you type, including each source's Recycle Bin. Source and move folders must be inside a mapped folder and outside the app data folder, and invalid saved folders are reset when the settings load. - Folder picker fixes: a message when no folder is mapped, browsing from the top level works, and the move folder check refreshes after Browse. - Security: scripts using HTTP basic auth now count toward the failed-login lockout, malformed requests get a clear error instead of a server error, and statistics can no longer be corrupted when several saves happen at once.

Config.Name: App data
Config.Description: Settings, history, statistics and logs. Keep the Container Path /data.

Config.Name: Folder to scan
Config.Description: The share to scan (read/write), e.g. /mnt/user/downloads. Keep the Container Path /downloads.

Config.Name: Trash folder (optional)
Config.Description: Optional, e.g. /mnt/user/trash. If set, processed archives and junk are moved here. Otherwise they go to the share's .Recycle.Bin (Unraid Recycle Bin plugin) or are deleted - see Settings. Must not be inside the folder to scan (or a parent of it). Keep the Container Path /trash.

Config.Name: All shares (optional)
Config.Description: Optional, e.g. /mnt/user. Lets the web UI browse and extract any share (Extract folder button, folder pickers) and reach each share's .Recycle.Bin. Gives the container read/write access to all your shares, so leave it empty unless you need it. Keep the Container Path /mnt/user.

Config.Name: Timezone
Config.Description: Timezone for the times shown in logs.

Config.Name: UI username
Config.Description: Login name for the web UI (only used when a password is set). Default admin.

Config.Name: UI password
Config.Description: Set a password to require a login for the web UI. Blank = no login.
